1-15231-2-1.subevent: A mortar attack occurred in northern Faryab province on Thursday morning.
At least four civilians were killed and 10 others were wounded in the attack.
The incident happened around 11:00am local time after a mortar round landed in a market in Shareen Tagab district.
Abdul Karim Yourish, a spokesman for the provincial police chief, said the mortar was fired by the Taliban to target security forces, but all the victims were civilians at the market.
The Taliban has not commented on the attack.

0-4495-1-1.subevent: Tunisia Youth Impact uses Voticook cooking contests to encourage women in rural villages to vote in the presidential election.
The contest takes place on October 12 in Echamine, ahead of the second round on October 13, amid low turnout in the first round.
The contest mimics real voting conditions, with women competing by preparing dishes and diners voting for the winner as a practice vote.
The event is held at the home of Hinda Jlass, who prepares couscous and plans to vote on Sunday for only the second time.
Seven women compete, presenting their dishes to about fifty electors, who taste and vote using the same procedure as the real election.
Tunisia Youth Impact volunteers guide voters through the process, with members of the ISIE and EU observer Stefan Ziegler present.
After voting, ballots are counted and volunteers point out mistakes that could invalidate a vote.
Najwa Jlass wins the contest and says she will vote in the real election.

6-18979-2-t.subevent: Crime adapts to society; modern organized crime differs from the past, with the Sicilian Cosa Nostra adjusting to an urban-industrial economy.
Organized crime forms networks across national boundaries, linking criminals with legitimate institutions.
Drug trafficking leads to corruption, violence, money laundering, and intertwines common, economic, and organized crimes.
Organized criminals seek a power monopoly, operating without regard for public interest or legal rules.
Common crime and organized crime intersect but are distinguished by organizational characteristics like hierarchy and continuity.
Organized crime develops a mythology of invincibility, and affiliates use this to intimidate; mafia hits signal internal conflicts.
Defining organized crime is difficult; informants' testimonies have provided documentation, as in the case of Italian groups.

Nigerian criminal enterprises, with three structural types, are pervasive globally, engaging in heroin trafficking and scams such as the '419' advance fee fraud and check theft, with proceeds funding narcotics.

13-wiki-img/24416-1/24416-1-1.subevent: The State Emergency Commission held a meeting today.

The State Emergency Commission decided to suspend all movements of automobiles, buses, and railway but air transport between Ulaanbaatar and 21 aimags from 08.00 am of February 23 to 08.00 am of February 27, during the Tsagaan Sar Holiday.

0-4931-1-4.subevent: The police helicopter crashed into the Clutha bar on 29 November 2013, killing 10 people and injuring 31.

Sheriff Turnbull concluded that the crash was caused by Captain Traill ignoring five low fuel warnings, as the fuel tanks were depleted because he failed to ensure at least one fuel transfer pump switch was on.
Sheriff Turnbull stated that the accident would not have happened if the pilot had followed the normal procedure for low fuel warnings.
Sheriff Turnbull described the pilot's failure as 'inexplicable' and said he took a chance the warnings were erroneous.
Sheriff Turnbull said the helicopter should have had a warning when both fuel pumps were off, but the circumstances were unlikely to be repeated.
Sheriff Turnbull criticized the delay in the inquiry and said the Crown Office's team was not sufficiently resourced.
The Crown Office acknowledged the delay and said improvements were being made.
Airbus Helicopters expressed sadness and commitment to safety.
Victims' family and the pub owner expressed anger and shock at the inquiry's findings.

3-17441-15-t.subevent: Confindustria forecast a 6% GDP fall and a serious recession in 2020.
Economy Minister Gualtieri said the forecast is realistic and Italy can aim for a vigorous rebound.
The government will publish its own economic estimates in the Document of Economy and Finance at the end of April.
Italy's GDP grew 0.3% in 2019, and the government had expected 0.6% growth in 2020 before the coronavirus outbreak emerged in late February.
At the end of March, sources said the Treasury expected the economy to contract about 3% this year.

Gualtieri said a new stimulus package, to be approved in April, would be significantly larger than the 25 billion euros passed in March and sufficient to support companies and households for the entire epidemic.
Gualtieri said the package would include extended state-backed guarantees, unemployment benefits, and support for low-income people.
Gualtieri said the European Stability Mechanism was not an option under current conditions, and that Europe needed a coordinated fiscal policy and new solutions.

21-31050-3-1.subevent: Yoshiro Mori resigned as president of the Tokyo Olympic Committee at a board meeting on Friday.
His resignation followed outcry over his earlier remarks that women talk too much and have a strong sense of rivalry, for which he apologized and retracted.
Upon resigning, Mori apologized again but said his comments were misinterpreted and he is not prejudiced against women.
IOC President Thomas Bach issued a statement respecting Mori's decision and pledging continued cooperation.
The controversy added to existing challenges for the Tokyo Games, including the pandemic, ballooning costs, public opposition, and a change in prime minister.
Hundreds of Olympic volunteers quit and local organizers received thousands of complaints, while athletes Naomi Osaka and Kosuke Hagino criticized Mori and sponsors voiced concerns.
The controversy highlighted sexism and gender inequality in Japan's male-dominated elite, with female lawmakers protesting.
Experts commented that the public strongly rejected Mori's remarks, but the pandemic will likely be the main legacy of the Games.

33-2542-7-1.subevent: Marines splashed a hostile Iranian drone using the Marine Air Defense Integrated System (MADIS) on the deck of USS Boxer during a transit through the Strait of Hormuz.

MADIS is a combination of electronic jammers, radars, and gun systems; the version used was mounted on an MRZR and powered by a gasoline generator; the Marine Corps did not immediately respond to a request for additional information.
The encounter is the first known kill by a new generation of electronic warfare and directed energy weapons, according to naval analyst Thomas Callender.

The Navy and Marine Corps have been concerned about swarms of cheap unmanned vehicles; firing expensive missiles like the RIM-7 Sea Sparrow ($170,000) or RIM-116 ($1 million) to intercept drones puts the U.S. at a cost disadvantage.
The Navy has tested less expensive options like 5-inch deck guns and Phalanx CIWS, but they required multiple shots and still cost thousands of dollars.
In 2014, the Navy deployed a 30-kilowatt laser aboard a ship in the Persian Gulf as an early test of directed energy weapons, costing about a dollar per shot.
The Navy plans to install a 60-kilowatt HELIOS directed energy weapon on a destroyer in 2021 and is developing SEWIP Block III electronic attack capabilities.
Using systems like MADIS is less escalatory and could provide deniability, according to Callender.

1-15230-2-1.subevent: Hamida, a 10-year-old girl in Bamyan, helps with potato harvest and started attending school last year after never having been to school before.
According to Unicef, 3.2 million girls are now getting an education in Afghanistan, a dramatic rise since the US-led invasion ended the Taliban ban on girls' schooling in 2001.
The female literacy rate has tripled but remains at about 13%, one of the world's lowest, and conservative attitudes and practices like child marriages and abuse persist.

Gulnaz was raped by her cousin's husband, charged with adultery, gave birth in jail, and was pardoned by President Karzai after international outcry; Karzai has faced criticism from women's groups for not taking a stronger stand.
At Suriya school in Kabul, girls practice cricket with a male coach, unimaginable under the Taliban; UK charity Afghan Connection provides equipment and Marylebone Cricket Club also supports.
A 12-year-old girl at the school expresses a desire to become a journalist.
Outside major cities, changes are patchy: 60% of the 4.2 million out-of-school children are girls, mostly in rural and conflict-affected areas, and the Taliban have forced many schools to close.

There is anxiety about the momentum of change after US withdrawal in 2014, but Education Minister Farooq Wardak insists it will continue, and Afghan Connection's Dr. Sarah Fayne believes the changes are permanent because parents who have let their daughters go to school will not allow that to be taken away.
Hamida's mother, who had no school in her time, hopes Hamida's dream of becoming a doctor comes true.

6-19726-1-1.subevent: Biomerieux gave its proprietary formula to the Canadian government for free so its national lab can try to manufacture coronavirus test kit chemicals.
Canada passed emergency legislation in March that allowed the government to produce patented goods without the patent holders’ consent.
Biomerieux did not respond to questions about similar arrangements with other governments, and reported a 21.5% increase in sales in the first quarter partly due to demand for reagent.
The Public Health Agency of Canada described the arrangement as a temporary license at no cost, with manufacturing still in development.

Biomerieux’s Canadian unit emailed customers in early April saying the move was meant to clear testing backlogs and that it was also boosting its own production, expressing hope that it would allow more Canadians to be tested.
The chemicals, called reagents, used to extract RNA from patient samples are in short supply, and suppliers including Thermo Fisher and Roche face soaring demand.
Biomerieux equipment is widely used in Canada, and heavy reliance on one brand contributed to a testing slowdown in late March.
PHAC said the deal is an interim solution, and Canada pledged C$1.1 billion for research and drug or vaccine manufacturing.

9-21075-1-t.subevent: O Governo divulgou a lista final de atividades que têm de fechar a partir de sexta-feira, às 0h00.
As escolas de condução só podem abrir para a realização de provas e exames.
Os centros de explicações e escolas de línguas foram incluídos na lista de encerramento.
As atividades de ocupação de tempos livres têm de fechar.
Atividades recreativas, de lazer e diversão como discotecas, bares, circos, parques de diversões e jardins zoológicos são encerradas.
Atividades culturais e artísticas como auditórios, cinemas, teatros, museus, bibliotecas e galerias de arte são encerradas.
Atividades desportivas em recintos fechados, incluindo ginásios, academias, estádios e piscinas, são encerradas, com exceções para treinos de alta competição.
Restaurantes e similares são encerrados, exceto para entrega ao domicílio e take-away.
Ficam abertos estabelecimentos como supermercados, farmácias, hotéis, papelarias, e outros serviços essenciais listados.

1-14903-2-2.subevent: Widespread looting, arson, attacks on police stations and vehicles, destruction of an ambulance, and daily protests ending in clashes with security forces have occurred in Chile.
President Sebastian Pinera sends an urgent bill to Congress to allow the army to safeguard key installations and police stations without declaring a state of emergency.
The government states that about one-third of the estimated $1.5 billion in destruction since protests began was caused by criminal gangs, common criminals, drug traffickers, and anarchists.
Protesters Mario and Maria express anger, saying that peaceful protests have achieved nothing and that the rich and powerful threw the first stone through discrimination and neglect of basic needs.
Better-off Chilean Maria Olga says that the people causing destruction cannot be Chileans and she does not recognize the country.
Mario and Maria describe themselves as radical opponents of the system with no political affiliation, seeking only basic things like decent income and services.
A new study shows that 58 percent of Chileans belong to the lower-middle-class or vulnerable class unable to access basic needs under the current system.
Many protesters, including Mario, distrust political institutions and the elite, rejecting voting and feeling unrepresented by parties.

0-4407-1-1.subevent: A double-decker bus overturned into a field on the A385 between Totnes and Paignton, Devon, at around 11am on Saturday 5 October.
Emergency services declared a major incident and adopted a multi-agency approach, deploying police, fire, ambulance, and air ambulances to the scene.
At 5:30pm, Devon and Cornwall Police released a statement that 37 people sustained injuries, of which eight are described as having potentially serious injuries.
The police confirmed that the road will close again from 7am on Sunday 6 October while emergency crews recover the bus from the field.
The police added that there is significant pressure on local health services as a result of the crash and urged people not to attend A&E departments unless it is a real emergency.

1-14955-1-t.subevent: President Trump pointed to a bar chart showing Belgium's coronavirus death toll per capita exceeded all other countries, and that the U.S. rate was below six European nations.
Belgian minister Denis Ducarme criticized Trump's display as 'macabre' and 'level zero' politics.
Ducarme defended Belgium's counting method as 'the most exhaustive possible.'
Belgian authorities decided to include not only confirmed COVID-19 deaths but also suspected ones, whether tested or not.
As of Wednesday, Belgium counted 6,262 COVID-19 deaths (roughly 540 per million), with more than half in nursing homes and only 4.5% of those confirmed infected.
Belgian authorities came under pressure to change their method, and Prime Minister Sophie Wilmès suggested the count has been exaggerated.
Spokesman Emmanuel André defended the method, insisting other governments have been undercounting and that more countries are copying Belgium's model.
André said, 'When you don't know, it's more difficult to act.'
Experts said Belgium likely hit the coronavirus peak on April 12, and a special task force is due to unveil a gradual exit strategy on Friday.

7-36661-5-2.subevent: The Technical University of Denmark has been shut down, but Professor Anders Wolff continues working on the CoronaDX project.
Project partner Professor Anders Fomsgaard from Statens Seruminstitut also continues working.
Two of the three instruments are scheduled to be ready for emergency use in October 2020, and the third in March 2021.
The fastest instrument will give a diagnosis in less than one minute; the slowest in less than an hour.
The instruments are designed to be easy to use, like a pregnancy test, enabling on-site testing and reducing pressure on central laboratories.
Professor Fomsgaard states that the speed and ease of use could increase the effectiveness of the healthcare system’s response to future epidemics.
Under normal conditions, such development would take years, but the project is developing unusually fast due to collaboration and publicly available COVID-19 RNA sequences.
The three instruments measure in three different ways, and the technology was recently developed for detecting diseases in poultry.

The researchers need to develop new reagents; they are allowed to test equipment in the field early, and their Chinese partners will test two instruments in China in June, with an expected emergency use permit in Denmark in October.

2-35026-1-t.subevent: France seized the British scallop dredger Cornelis Gert Jan and escorted it to Le Havre, and a second British vessel received a verbal warning.
France listed potential sanctions against Britain, including extra customs checks from Nov. 2 and a threat to cut electricity exports if talks fail.
French minister Annick Girardin said 'It's not war, but it is a fight.'
Britain denounced France's reaction as 'disappointing and disproportionate' and warned that threatened steps would be met with a calibrated response.
France's European Affairs Minister Clement Beaune said they need to speak the language of strength, while Girardin clarified France could not cut electricity but could raise tariffs.
The Cornelis Gert Jan's skipper was placed under preliminary investigation for dredging scallops and could face a fine, while the vessel's owners claimed they had a fishing license.
Observers noted that France appeared determined to escalate the license row before the presidential election, and 15 license requests from Boulogne moved to 'under consideration' after the seizure.
Senior officials signaled they did not want escalation, but leaders were under pressure from fishing lobbies and wanted to show they were defending voters' interests.
In Le Havre, French scallop fishermen complained about British vessels having unfair access to shellfish in French waters.

0-4882-1-2.subevent: The X-37B Mission 5 landed at NASA's Kennedy Space Center Shuttle Landing Facility on Oct. 27, 2019, after 780 days in orbit, breaking its own endurance record.
The total days spent on-orbit for the entire X-37B program reached 2,865 days.
Secretary of the Air Force Barbara Barrett stated that the X-37B demonstrates the importance of a reusable spaceplane.
Air Force Chief of Staff Gen. David L. Goldfein praised the safe return and the partnership between government and industry.
The X-37B program, managed by the Air Force Rapid Capabilities Office, performs risk reduction, experimentation, and concept of operations development for reusable space vehicle technologies.
Randy Walden, director of the Air Force Rapid Capabilities Office, said the mission completed its longest flight and successfully hosted experiments and small satellites.
Lt. Col. Jonathan Keen, X-37B program manager, called the spacecraft a key component and said the milestone demonstrates commitment to future space exploration.
The X-37B landed at Kennedy Space Center for the second time; Mission 4 landed after 718 days, and the vehicle was designed for 270-day missions.
The fifth mission launched on Sept. 7, 2017, from Cape Canaveral, and the Air Force is preparing for the sixth mission in 2020.

9-21348-5-1.subevent: Central Americans leave their homes due to armed violence, including killings, gang recruitment, rape, police harassment, and death threats.
Historically, Central Americans migrated for economic reasons after civil wars displaced millions in the 1970s and 1980s.
Today's migrant flow includes more families, children, and pregnant women fleeing life-or-death situations, not just poverty.
The 1996 U.S. Illegal Immigration Reform and Immigrant Responsibility Act led to deportations that expanded gangs like MS-13 and Barrio 18 in Central America.
Civil wars, inequality, mass incarceration, and weak institutions created a severe gang problem in the region.
Parents in gang-controlled 'red zones' spend extra money on private transport or after-school programs to protect their children from gangs.
Gangs gradually recruit children as young as 12, starting with gifts and parties, and may force families to leave their homes for strategic use.
Gangs remain undefeated despite police operations, and government crackdowns sometimes make residents fear police more than gangs.
Many Central Americans decide to flee to the U.S. despite dangers because staying in their home countries is a life-or-death situation.

0-4546-1-2.subevent: Three people died in two Southern California wildfires.
The Saddleridge Fire ignited late Thursday in Sylmar, destroying more than 30 structures and burning over 7,900 acres by Saturday night, with 33% containment.
Governor Newsom and Mayor Garcetti issued emergency declarations, with Newsom securing a FEMA grant.
Over 1,000 firefighters battled the fire, which was fueled by strong Santa Ana winds, causing freeway closures.
Evacuation orders affected communities on both sides of Interstate 5, and 276 minors were evacuated from a juvenile detention center while a hospital was under shelter-in-place.
One civilian died from cardiac arrest and one firefighter sustained a minor eye injury.
The Sandalwood Fire in Riverside County was 68% contained at 1,000 acres, with two deaths and 74 structures destroyed.
Power companies PG&E and Southern California Edison preemptively shut off power to customers in several counties due to high winds.
SoCalGas tweeted that there were no indications of damage or leaks at the Aliso Canyon facility.

1-15178-2-1.subevent: Portugal's Catholic bishops announced the suspension of public Masses from Jan. 23 due to the extreme gravity of the pandemic.
Portugal was experiencing a surge in COVID-19 deaths, with 609,000 cases and 9,920 deaths as of Jan. 22.
This was the second suspension of public worship; the first occurred in March 2020 and was lifted at the end of May.
The suspension included public Masses, catechesis, and other pastoral activities, and bishops urged priests to livestream Masses.
Earlier in January, the bishops had called for the suspension or postponement of baptisms, confirmations, and marriages.
Funerals could be celebrated with social distancing norms issued in May 2020.
A Lenten retreat for the bishops scheduled for Feb. 22-26 was canceled.
The Shrine of Our Lady of Fatima announced it would broadcast three Masses and two rosaries daily during the suspension.
Shrine rector Fr. Carlos Cabecinhas acknowledged the difficulty of virtual participation.

1-14989-2-3.subevent: A new study concludes that the megatooth shark Otodus megalodon was the largest shark to ever swim in the oceans.
O. megalodon lived approximately 23 to 3.6 million years ago, and the exact cause of its extinction is debated.
Little is known about the life-appearance of megalodon because sharks have cartilaginous skeletons that decay, leaving only teeth.
A previous study estimated that a full-grown megalodon could reach about 50 feet (15 meters) in length.
A new study published in Historical Biology compiled a database of 70 shark species and used measurements of present-day sharks to infer the body size of extinct species over geologic time.
The study found that non-planktivorous sharks have a general size limit of 23 feet (7 meters), and only a few plankton-eating sharks reach 26 to 32 feet (8 to 10 meters).

The study also found that sharks on average got bigger in the last 65 million years, but with a maximum size of 46 to 50 feet, O. megalodon was exceptionally large, likely the maximum size for sharks.
Warm-bloodedness and oophagy (cannibalistic egg-eating) are proposed adaptations that enable gigantism in sharks, and based on growth models, a newborn megalodon was already 9 feet (3 meters) long.

10-6887-1-2.subevent: Dozens of climate activists invaded BlackRock’s office in Paris, calling for the fund to pull out of fossil fuel investments.
The activists entered the building, reached the fourth floor, and graffitied walls with tags like 'I want to live' and 'Murderers'.
They blocked the entrance with ropes and rolling office cabinets before riot police arrived.
A 15-year-old Fridays for Future member, Emilia, said they want to change the capitalistic system.
BlackRock condemned the violent intrusion and acts of vandalism in a statement.
BlackRock CEO Larry Fink warned company boards in January to step up efforts to tackle climate change.
Fink said his firm would exit investments with high sustainability-related risk, including thermal coal producers.
Extinction Rebellion had previously targeted Shell’s headquarters, McKinsey’s London office, and staged a demonstration at a Brussels car show.

11-23153-1-1.subevent: Zanzibar's first vice President and ACT Wazalendo's Chairman Maalim Seif Sharif Hamad died at the age of 77.
He was admitted to Muhimbili National Hospital (MNH) in Dar es Salaam on February 9, 2021.
He died on Wednesday, February 17, 2021 at 11:26 in the morning.
He had been hospitalized at Mnazi Mmoja Hospital in Zanzibar on January 31 after he allegedly tested positive for Coronavirus.
Zanzibar President Hussein Mwinyi announced his death on February 17 and declared seven days of national mourning.
President John Magufuli sent condolences to Zanzibar's President and the people of Zanzibar via Twitter.

1-15800-4-1.subevent: Tropical Depression 5 strengthened into Tropical Storm Edouard at 11 p.m. EDT on July 5.
On July 6 at 1:45 a.m. EDT, NASA's Aqua satellite analyzed Tropical Storm Edouard's cloud tops in infrared light.
The MODIS instrument found a small area of powerful thunderstorms northeast of the center with cloud top temperatures as cold as minus 70 degrees Fahrenheit.
Southwesterly wind shear pushed the strongest storms northeast of the center, leaving an exposed swirl of low- to mid-level clouds.
At 5 a.m. EDT on July 6, Edouard was centered about 530 miles south of Cape Race, Newfoundland, with maximum sustained winds near 40 mph and a minimum central pressure of 1008 millibars.
Little significant change in strength was forecast before Edouard becomes post-tropical later in the day.
Edouard was moving northeast at 36 mph, expected to continue toward the United Kingdom.

National Hurricane Center forecaster Jack Beven noted that the cyclone is in strong southwesterly wind shear, heading for colder water, and approaching a frontal system, leading to extratropical transition within 12 to 24 hours with possible slight strengthening, after which the extratropical low should persist for about 24 hours before dissipating.

0-4813-2.subevent: Lion Air crash killed 189 people and was caused by failures by Boeing, Lion Air, and pilots.
Ethiopian Airlines crash killed 157 people, leading to the grounding of the entire 737 Max fleet.
Indonesian investigators released a final report detailing the list of events that caused the crash.
The report found the jet should have been grounded due to an unrecorded cockpit issue, a sensor was not properly tested, and the MCAS software repeatedly pushed the plane nose down.
The report identified pilot errors including a poorly performing first officer and a captain who failed to brief him properly, and noted 31 pages missing from the maintenance log.
Boeing responded by addressing recommendations, planning to redesign MCAS, ousting Kevin McAllister as CEO of Boeing Commercial Airplanes, and expecting 737 Max recertification by year's end.

Revelations emerged that Boeing employees exchanged messages about MCAS issues during certification, a pilot had lied to regulators, the company's profits halved, and its CEO Dennis Muilenburg was stripped of his chairman title.

1-16084-3-1.subevent: International aid organizations and doctors sound alarm over coronavirus threat to overcrowded Greek refugee camps.
An outbreak of the disease occurs at two facilities near Athens, intensifying concerns for the 36,000 people stranded on Aegean islands.
Dutch physician Steven van de Vijver launches an online petition urging EU leaders to take in refugees from Greece, which gains over 6,000 signatures from European doctors.
Greek authorities quarantine the Malakasa camp after an Afghan refugee shows symptoms and seal off the Ritsona camp after 23 African asylum seekers test positive.
Migration ministry secretary Manos Logothetis states that all symptomatic cases are isolated and testing continues, but acknowledges challenges.
The outbreak is traced to a 19-year-old Cameroonian woman infected after giving birth; Logothetis notes all other cases are asymptomatic due to young population.
NGOs express fears over lack of access to testing, medical facilities, and basic services in island camps, and call for evacuation of refugees to other EU countries.
Doctors warn that coronavirus is almost certain to strike the island camps, citing poor conditions at places like the Moria camp where scabies, pneumonia, and diarrhoea are rife.
Greek officials describe the camps as "ticking health bombs" and call on EU states to share the burden by taking in refugees, with Logothetis suggesting each member state take in 2,000 people.

2-34919-5-1.subevent: People arriving in Belgium are instructed to quarantine themselves at home for a fortnight.
Arrivals are also told to observe social distancing measures: the 'safe distance' in Belgium is 1.5 metres.
Arrivals aren’t allowed out to work outside the home for a fortnight.
Relatives or friends collecting arrivals also have to observe a quarantine.

4-35568-7-1.subevent: Belarusian President Lukashenko said it was 'absolutely possible' his forces helped migrants cross into the EU, but denied inviting them, as European governments accused Belarus of artificially creating the crisis.

Polish border guards reported attempted crossings by two groups, including one of 500 people who threw rocks and tear gas, aided by Belarusian authorities, and said they arrested 45 people; Al Jazeera noted it could not independently verify claims due to a ban on reporters.

Despite Minsk clearing main camps and allowing a repatriation flight to Iraq, aid groups said at least 11 asylum seekers and refugees have died on both sides of the border, and human rights groups accused Poland of exacerbating suffering by sending back those who try to cross.

Poland and its allies accused Belarus of deliberately enticing thousands of migrants in response to Western sanctions, while Minsk denied the claim and accused Polish forces of committing crimes against humanity.
Lukashenko and Russian President Vladimir Putin spoke by phone and stressed the importance of cooperation between Minsk and the EU to resolve the problem.

Ukraine announced it was preparing systematically for a possible shift of the crisis to its territory, with its interior minister warning that migrants who cross over would be pushed back with any means necessary, including firearms.
Polish Defense Minister Mariusz Blaszczak tweeted that Warsaw accepted Estonia's proposal to send 100 troops to the border.

Migrants from the camps were taken to a crowded warehouse; some expressed hope for Europe while a Syrian migrant in a Polish hospital described being threatened by the Belarusian army and said he feared being forcibly returned to Belarus.

Council of Europe human rights commissioner Dunja Mijatovic called the humanitarian situation alarming and demanded an end to pushbacks, as well as immediate and unimpeded access for rights activists and media; Belarus said there were about 7,000 migrants in the country.

0-4716-1-2.subevent: After four months of protest and repression, Chileans look ahead to a plebiscite that may open the way to a new Constitution.
General Augusto Pinochet's 1980 Constitution institutionalized an authoritarian neoliberal model that continues to shape Chilean politics and economics.
Privatizations of pensions, health, education, and water under the Constitution have perpetuated inequality and extreme social divisions.
President Sebastián Piñera declared 'We are at war' and deployed the army to enforce a curfew, evoking memories of the dictatorship.
On October 25, 1.2 million people gathered in Santiago's Plaza Italia to protest, chanting 'Chile woke up.'
International human rights delegations criticized security forces for excessive force, and the UN expressed alarm over an 'anti-looting law' criminalizing protest tactics.
The demonstrations mark a new era of social struggle with broad participation, youth involvement, and cultural expressions such as songs and murals.
The upcoming plebiscite offers hope for ending the neoliberal system, but the outcome remains uncertain as Piñera resists structural change.

0-4472-6-1.subevent: Ecuador halted Latin America's shift to the right when Lenín Moreno defeated former banker Guillermo Lasso in the presidential election.
Moreno, a 64-year-old paraplegic who served as vice president under Rafael Correa, promised to be president of everyone, especially the poor.
Correa, president from 2007 to 2013, brought stability and social programs that lifted many out of poverty.
Ecuador's economy suffered due to falling oil prices and a devastating earthquake in 2016, which the opposition blamed on Correa.
Lasso was part of Jamil Mahuad's government during a banking crisis that caused misery, emigration, and currency collapse, which Correa later declared immoral and refused to pay.
Voters rejected Lasso because of his past involvement in the economic crisis and his proposed cuts to social spending and tax reductions for the rich.
Lasso disputed the election results, but international observers confirmed no fraud, and the OAS and several countries recognized Moreno's victory.
Correa said he left the country in good hands, and Moreno tweeted a message of unity.

2-34752-6-2.subevent: The article discusses how various climate impacts might affect harmful algal blooms.
Toxic blue-green algae thrive in warm, slow-moving water, and warmer water due to climate change favors harmful algae.
Climate change might lead to more droughts, making freshwater saltier and causing marine algae to invade freshwater ecosystems.
Higher levels of carbon dioxide in the air and water can lead to rapid growth of algae, especially toxic blue-green algae.
Climate change might affect rainfall patterns, leading to alternating periods of drought and intense storms that cause more nutrient runoff and feed more algal blooms.
Sea level rise could create more shallow and stable coastal water, conditions that are perfect for the growth of algae.
Climate change is expected to alter the timing and intensity of coastal upwelling, which might lead to more algal blooms along the west coast of the United States.

1-15885-8-t.subevent: On Jan. 10, 2020, the SARS-CoV-2 sequence data was shared through the GISAID Initiative.
On March 11, 2020, the World Health Organization declared COVID-19 a pandemic.
On March 19, 2020, the research-based global pharmaceutical industry committed to address COVID-19.
In April 2020, the first human clinical trial for a COVID-19 vaccine was conducted.
On April 24, 2020, the IFPMA joined the Access to COVID-19 Tools Accelerator, leading to the COVAX facility.
On Sept. 8, 2020, nine vaccine makers pledged a united commitment to rigorous scientific and regulatory processes.
On Dec. 31, 2020, the Pfizer/BioNTech vaccine received WHO Emergency Use Listing, followed by the AstraZeneca/Oxford vaccine on Feb. 15, 2021.
In the first quarter of 2021, COVAX began the rollout of two billion doses of vaccines to lower-middle-income countries via UNICEF.

16-10208-2-1.subevent: The city of Mönchengladbach announced on Tuesday morning that Borussia and 1. FC Köln will play without fans on Wednesday evening.
The decision to play without spectators was made in reaction to the spread of the coronavirus.
Federal Health Minister Jens Spahn had repeatedly recommended canceling events with more than 1000 spectators.
The DFL is examining the possibility of adjusting the licensing procedure for the 2020/21 season to account for financial disadvantages from the coronavirus.
The DFL is considering adjusting payout dates of centrally generated revenue to relieve clubs in case of liquidity bottlenecks.
