1-16438-6-t.subevent: WFSA is working with its global membership to curate, share, and disseminate up-to-date and practical COVID-19 guidance for anaesthesia and perioperative care providers.
WFSA drew attention to the particular risk for anaesthesiologists and other perioperative care providers when providing respiratory care and tracheal intubation of patients with COVID-19.
WFSA released a statement on health care provider safety and wellbeing during the COVID-19 pandemic.
Several organizations, including APSF, ASA, IARS, and others, provided perioperative considerations and guidelines for patients with suspected or confirmed COVID-19.
Guidance on airway management for COVID-19 patients was published by SIAARTI, Prince of Wales Hospital Hong Kong, and UCSF.
Guidance on obstetric anaesthesia related to COVID-19 was provided by SOAP, RCOG, and other organizations.
WFSA curated a page of specific guidance for anesthesia providers working in low-resource settings.
WFSA member societies, such as the Indian Society of Anaesthesiologists and the South African Society of Anaesthesiologists, issued their own advisories and guidelines.
Resources in French, Spanish, Portuguese, and general information from WHO, CDC, and MSF were compiled and made available.

1-14823-1-1.subevent: This week, negotiating mandates were set out, with the EU wanting little change and the UK seeking a radical re-drawing of 40 years of fisheries management.
The UK government published its negotiating mandate on Thursday, proposing annual negotiations and rejecting 'relative stability' in favor of 'zonal attachment.'
The EU's chief negotiator Michel Barnier emphasized fisheries in the context of a free trade deal, wanting to uphold existing access and quota shares, and linking access to EU markets.

In the Scottish Parliament, Fergus Ewing set out measures to improve inshore fleet relations and highlighted the sector's significance, noting that 80% of Scotland's vessels operate inshore and £100m of langoustines were exported in 2018.
The inshore fleet and fish processors expressed fears about health certificates and bottlenecks at Channel ports that could harm exports of fresh catch to France and Spain.
Both sides agreed on the need for a deal by summer to set new annual catch quotas, with the UK prepared to increase patrol boats to exclude EU fishers if no deal is reached.
The UK proposal separates fish catch in UK waters from fish sales in EU markets, aiming to include trade in fisheries products under a Comprehensive Free Trade Agreement.
The EU uses access to its markets as leverage, stating that the terms on access shall guide other aspects of the economic partnership.
Brexiteers exploited dislike of the Common Fisheries Policy during the 2016 campaign, and Whitehall discussions described fisheries as 'expendable' alongside other priorities.

27-33401-5-2.subevent: Pangkogabwilhan II Marsdya TNI Imran Baidirus conducted a working visit to Poso to survey the situation via air as part of Operasi Tinombala 2020 on December 29, 2020.
After a flight briefing, he, accompanied by Pangkoopsau II Makassar Marsda TNI Minggit Tribowo and Asops Kaskogabwilhan II Brigjen TNI Bobby Rinal Makmun, boarded a Boeing aircraft.
They observed the situation in Poso and surrounding areas from the air using the aircraft.
The flight followed the route from Lanud Sultan Hasanuddin to Sas Palu to Sas Hnd.
The operation emphasizes law enforcement supported by intelligence, Binmas, and other police functions, and the Tinombala Task Force continues because many targets have not been captured.

0-4834-16-t.subevent: Demonstrators in Baghdad and mainly in Sadr City took to the streets on Thursday in denunciation of lack of services, unemployment and unfair apportionment.
Public sector employees joined residents in their rally.
Oil Minister employees called to be included in the staffing cadre just as their mates in other ministries.
Employees of the General groups firm related to the Ministry of Industry and minerals protested against the decision to cut off 20% of their salaries.
All Iraqis are united over the call to improve their situation, ascertain security in the country and boost its economy.

33-2389-1-1.subevent: YouTube announced it is removing videos that promote extremist views like white supremacy or deny events such as the Holocaust or the Sandy Hook shooting.
The new policy prohibits videos alleging that a group is superior to justify discrimination, segregation, or exclusion based on qualities like age, gender, race, religion, or sexual orientation.
YouTube refused to take down the channel of conservative personality Stephen Crowder after he used homophobic slurs against journalist Carlos Maza, stating the videos did not violate its policies.
YouTube said it would remove channels that approach its hate speech rules from its YouTube Partner Program and reduce the reach of other borderline content.
YouTube suspended monetization of Stephen Crowder's channel due to a pattern of egregious actions harming the community.
YouTube stated Crowder could regain monetization if he addressed certain issues, including removing a link to his merchandise from a video.
The new hate speech policy comes as platforms like YouTube, Facebook, and Twitter face intense scrutiny over their content moderation practices.
The Anti-Defamation League applauded YouTube's new policy but called for further changes to adequately counter online hate and extremism.

0-4488-1-1.subevent: Boko Haram launched its second attack on Maiduguri on February 1.
Nigerian troops repelled the attack and claimed to inflict hundreds of casualties.
Earlier in the year, Boko Haram captured the town of Baga and 16 surrounding villages.
After a previous failed attack on Maiduguri, Boko Haram captured the town of Monguno.
Reliable estimates of Boko Haram's strength do not exist, with experts estimating between 5,000 and 50,000 fighters.
The article deduces Boko Haram has a core strength of 7,000 to 10,000 fighters, noting that more than 10,000 would have taken Maiduguri.
Boko Haram likely has an additional 10,000 press-ganged auxiliaries used as cannon fodder.
Nigeria, Cameroon, and Chad have deployed 35,000 troops, which might block advances, but the insurgency's terrain and support, as well as opaque finances, pose challenges.

1-14826-2-13.subevent: Alicia Soto attended the 1 October Sunrise Remembrance Ceremony, describing her emotional scars and her reason for returning.
Since the shooting, Soto has moved to Minneapolis, started her dream job as a flight attendant, and decided to live life to the fullest for those who died.
A slideshow displayed the names and pictures of the 58 people killed, with two additional women who died within the past year included with a message.

Clark County Sheriff Joe Lombardo announced that Kimberly Gervais and Samanta Arjune will be added to the official death toll, raising it to 60, and later said he was comfortable acknowledging them as victims.

The ceremony had fewer attendees due to the coronavirus pandemic, and Gov. Steve Sisolak, who addressed the crowd, said that the event was one of his biggest priorities after raising the limit on public gatherings.
Sisolak's voice grew shaky as he recalled the night and said, 'We will never, never forget what happened that day.'

Albert Rivera, father of victim Jordyn Rivera, expressed gratitude to survivors and other supporters, acknowledged Greg Zanis, and ended by calling for unity and remembering how people came together after the attack.

0-4716-1-1.subevent: The social uprising in Chile reached its fourth month, with masses continuing to protest and demand structural change despite ferocious repression by the militarized Carabineros police force.
Chileans look ahead to a plebiscite that may open the way to a new Constitution, replacing the Pinochet-era charter that has been a major obstacle to change.

General Augusto Pinochet's 1980 Constitution institutionalized economic and political domination, enshrined a neoliberal framework, restricted political participation, and gave the Right disproportionate power.
The Constitution locked in privatized pension, health, and water systems, perpetuating inequality and social divisions, with strict amendment rules requiring supermajorities.

President Sebastián Piñera declared 'We are at war' and deployed army troops to patrol streets and enforce a curfew, evoking memories of the dictatorship; the crackdown spurred massive demonstrations, including 1.2 million people on October 25.
International human rights delegations criticized the security forces for excessive use of force and deliberate intent to harm protesters.

The protests highlighted Chile's entrenched inequality, including income gaps, privatized public services, and a metro fare hike that sparked the uprising, with chants of 'It's not 30 pesos, it's 30 years!'
The demonstrations featured broad-based participation, new forms of autonomous mobilization, feminist actions (including the anthem 'El violador eres tú'), songs, murals, and memorials.
Piñera resisted structural change and pushed a 'security agenda'; Congress passed an 'anti-looting law' criminalizing protest tactics, which the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights criticized.

The upcoming plebiscite's outcome remains uncertain; protesters hope for a new constitution and end to the neoliberal system, while fearing no change, and the struggle has implications for Latin America and the world.

6-19306-4-t.subevent: The Northern Ireland economy is now highly unlikely to recover all the output lost in the last recession before the next one begins.
New official figures show that in the final quarter of 2019 the economy was still 4% smaller than its 2007 peak.
The Northern Ireland economy is now facing a deep recession as a result of the ongoing coronavirus crisis.
The Ulster University Economic Policy Centre estimated that output could fall by almost 10% in 2020.
Official figures from Nisra suggest the Northern Ireland economy grew by 0.7% in 2019.
That 0.7% growth compares to GDP growth of 1.4% for the UK as a whole in the same period.
The Northern Ireland economy was already slowing before the coronavirus crisis began.
Quarterly growth in the last three months of 2019 was just 0.2%, driven by the public sector and manufacturing, while the service sector showed no growth.

Nisra said official statistical evidence of the scale of the economic crisis will only be clear when the figures for the second quarter of 2020 are compiled, which are not due for release until October.

1-16475-1-1.subevent: An ancient gold coin described as a 'naked and shameless celebration' of the assassination of Julius Caesar sold for £2.7 million ($3.5 million) to an anonymous bidder, setting a new record for a coin sold at auction.
The coin features a portrait of Marcus Junius Brutus, the daggers used by Brutus and Cassius to kill Caesar, and a cap of Liberty, and is inscribed with 'Eid Mar' referencing the Ides of March.
The coin was issued by Brutus two years after the assassination in 42 BC.
Richard Beale, managing director of Roma Numismatics, described the coin as a 'naked and shameless celebration' of the assassination.

Caesar's death was fueled by the belief among Roman politicians that he intended to make himself king, and he was killed by a group of senators, including friends and people he had previously pardoned.
Brutus killed himself after losing the Battle of Philippi to Caesar's nephew Octavius and friend Mark Antony.
The coin is in near-mint condition and is one of only three known to exist.

The previous record for a Roman coin was a bronze sestertius of Emperor Hadrian sold for $2.5 million in 2008, and the record for any coin was an ancient Greek gold stater sold for $3.25 million in 2012.

0-4450-1-2.subevent: A ship carrying migrants sank off the Italian island of Lampedusa, killing at least 13 people.
The boat overturned shortly after midnight in rough weather conditions.
Rescuers recovered the bodies of 13 women, some of whom were pregnant, from the water.
Twenty-two survivors were rescued, while eight children and other pregnant women were still missing.
The boat capsized after many passengers rushed to one side as rescue boats approached in response to an emergency call.
Authorities described the ship as an overloaded and already listing boat six nautical miles from Lampedusa.
The International Organization for Migration stated that the boat began its journey in Tunisia and carried Tunisian and western African migrants.

1-14826-2-14.subevent: Alicia Soto attended the 1 October Sunrise Remembrance Ceremony for the third year to process her trauma.
A slideshow displayed the names and pictures of the 58 killed, and included two women who died within the past year from their injuries.
Clark County Sheriff Joe Lombardo announced that the two women, Kimberly Gervais and Samanta Arjune, would be added to the official death toll, raising it to 60.
The announcement followed a Review-Journal article highlighting their deaths and Metro's initial decision not to include them.
Lombardo said in an interview that he is comfortable acknowledging the two additional deaths.
The ceremony had fewer attendees due to the pandemic, and Governor Sisolak prioritized it when raising public gathering limits.
Sisolak gave a speech in which he said 'We will never, never forget' and offered condolences.
Albert Rivera, father of victim Jordyn Rivera, thanked survivors and acknowledged Greg Zanis, who built 58 crosses and died in May.
Rivera called for unity and urged people to remember how they came together after the shooting.

0-4388-1-1.subevent: A report commissioned by Italy's parliamentary anti-mafia commission found that 13 million Italians live in 610 districts where the mafia exerts influence.
The report stated that even law-abiding citizens in those areas are conditioned by the mafia's capillary control.
Giuseppe Pisanu said the mafia is now silently prospering, moving from spectacular crimes to business and politics.
Censis found the highest concentration of people under mafia shadow in Agrigento (95.9%) and Naples (95%).
The four main mobs have an annual turnover of €130bn, but the 22% of Italians under their shadow produce only 14.6% of GDP and hold 12.4% of bank deposits.
In Catania and Palermo, 80% of shops allegedly pay protection money starting from €500 a month.
Suspicious fires in the four regions studied doubled to 8,441 a year between 1998 and 2007.

Investigators believe clans are investing profits outside the south, including in building work for Milan's Expo 2015 and in Rome, where a large number of bars have received expensive makeovers attributed to mob money.
Pisanu said mafias are getting better at investing overseas, and the 'Ndrangheta has offered financial services to Colombian cartels.

3-17632-4-t.subevent: Preparations are in place to receive 55 individuals, including 46 Malaysians, returning from Iran on Sunday.
Women and Family Minister Datuk Seri Rina Harun expressed satisfaction with preparations at the monitoring centre in Nilai.
Rina said the centre will house the returnees, expected to arrive at 10.30am, and also place 23 officers involved in the mission and crew members.
Rina stated that there are 46 Malaysians, eight Singaporeans, and one Indonesian among the returnees.

Rina said the Social Welfare Department will work with other agencies to take care of those at the centre, including preparing food and providing counselling, adopting the same standard operating procedure as the previous mission.
The government is bringing home 46 Malaysians stranded in Iran on a special flight scheduled to land at Kuala Lumpur International Airport 2 at 6.10am Sunday.
Deputy Foreign Minister Datuk Kamarudin Jaffar said the AirAsia flight departed Tehran at 11.45 am Saturday.

2-34597-1-1.subevent: NASA's Lucy mission launched from Cape Canaveral at 5:34 a.m. ET, and the team confirmed the spacecraft was safe and its solar arrays deployed.
Lucy will embark on a 12-year mission to explore Jupiter's Trojan asteroids for the first time, providing high-resolution images to help understand solar system formation.
NASA associate administrator Thomas Zurbuchen said the mission will tell us about the history of the solar system and the formation of outer planets.
There are about 7,000 Trojan asteroids, with the largest 160 miles across, and Lucy will fly by one main-belt asteroid and seven Trojans.
Lucy will use three gravity assists from Earth and is named after the Lucy fossil, with the hope of revealing the solar system's history.
The spacecraft features large solar arrays and three science instruments, built by over 500 engineers and scientists.
Lucy will fly by the asteroids at 15,000 mph and 600 miles away, providing four times better resolution than previous flybys.
After its primary mission, the team plans to propose an extended mission, and the spacecraft will remain in a stable orbit for over 100,000 years.

0-4448-1-1.subevent: The UAA AN-12 freighter on approach to Lviv disappeared from radar and attempted an emergency landing due to fuel exhaustion, crashing 0.8nm before the runway, killing five and injuring three.

Ukraine's SES reported the aircraft disappeared at 07:10L, a crew member called at 07:29L, the aircraft was located at 07:40L, and three bodies were found, three injured, and two missing later found dead.
Ukraine's Ministry of Infrastructure reported four killed, later corrected to five killed, with three injured, and a cargo of 10 tons.
The Mayor of Lviv stated the crew declared an emergency due to low fuel, and the cockpit was cut off with shifted cargo.
The NBAAI reported the emergency landing and opened an investigation into the accident that killed five.
On Oct 5, EASA revoked the airline's authorized third country operator status, effectively banning it from EU airspace.
On Oct 7, Ukraine's Ministry of Transport terminated the airline's Air Operator Certificate effective Oct 5.
On Oct 9, the NBAAI announced the formation of a special commission, recovery of black boxes, collection of data, and preliminary information about weather and flight plan.

On Dec 20, the NBAAI released their preliminary report detailing the final approach sequence, including the crew's failure to maintain proper speed and altitude, and the discovery that the glide slope and heading alarm flags were turned off.

1-wiki-img/15491-1/15491-1-2.subevent: Mars will be at its biggest and brightest as it aligns with Earth on the same side of the sun, an event known as opposition.
Opposition occurs every two years when Mars and the sun are on directly opposite sides of Earth, and all three bodies line up at roughly 11.30pm.
According to the Royal Observatory Greenwich, Mars will be at its best around 1am on Wednesday.
Astronomer Hannah Banyard said the last opposition in 2018 was difficult to see, but this time Mars has been easy to spot, rising earlier and getting high into the sky.
NASA describes opposition as a phenomenon where Mars and the sun appear on opposite sides of Earth, with Mars rising at sunset and setting at sunrise.
Despite cloudy weather, Mars should be visible through breaks and can be seen with the naked eye, though a four-inch telescope with 24-millimetre magnification reveals surface features.
The next time Mars will be this big and bright will be 2033.

2-34752-6-1.subevent: Warming water temperature promotes harmful algal blooms as toxic blue-green algae thrive in warmer water, which prevents mixing, allows faster floating, and further warms the water through absorption of sunlight.
Climate change may increase droughts, making freshwater saltier and allowing marine algae to invade freshwater ecosystems, as seen in the southwestern and south central United States since 2000.
Higher levels of carbon dioxide in the air and water can lead to rapid growth of algae, especially toxic blue-green algae that can float to the surface.
Climate change may alter rainfall patterns, causing alternating droughts and intense storms, which increase nutrient runoff into waterbodies and feed more algal blooms.
Scientists predict sea level could rise up to one meter by 2100, creating shallow, stable coastal waters ideal for algal growth.
Climate change is expected to change the timing and intensity of coastal upwelling, delivering excess nutrients that may lead to more algal blooms along the west coast of the United States.

6-wiki-img/18504-2/18504-2-1.subevent: The Chang'e-5 orbiter delivered a return module containing 1.731 kg of lunar samples to Earth on Dec. 16 before firing its engines for an extended deep space mission.
In March, the orbiter entered an intended orbit around Sun-Earth Lagrange point 1, where it conducted tests on orbit control and observations of the Earth and Sun.
New tracking data suggests Chang'e-5 has left its L1 orbit and is destined for a lunar flyby around September 9 Eastern time.
Amateur satellite trackers observed a possible orbit alteration on Aug. 30, and the Beijing Aerospace Flight Control Center has not provided an update on plans.
Potential maneuvers depend on remaining propellant and could include entering lunar orbit, heading for another Lagrange point, or flying by asteroid 469219 Kamoʻoalewa.
Deputy chief designer Jing Peng said a Venus visit is unlikely and the orbiter will likely stay at L1 or in the Earth-moon system.
The lunar samples are being analyzed, and applications for sample materials are open to domestic and international institutions.
NASA has no plans to trade Apollo lunar samples with Chang'e-5 samples, but chief scientist Jim Green expressed hope for future exchange.
China is planning a follow-up sample-return mission Chang'e-6 in 2024 with a French payload, and the Chang'e-4 Yutu-2 rover has covered 799 meters on the lunar far side over 33 lunar days.

23-13614-13-t.subevent: Over the past year, Israel has allowed little more than basic humanitarian aid into Gaza, and a ceasefire two months ago has led to slow progress in easing restrictions.

Raw sewage leaks from rusting pipes at a Gaza sewage pumping station, and it took months of negotiations for Israel to allow some spare parts, but most sewage cannot be treated and flows into the sea.
A fisherman says he must fish despite the sewage because he needs to make a living.
Most of Gaza's 1.5 million people rely on food aid and cannot enter or leave; tens of thousands have lost jobs and most industrial operations are stopped due to lack of raw materials and export ban.
The Pepsi plant manager says his store is empty and production has been drastically cut.
Some improvements since the truce include more fuel and limited other products, but the UN says they have not significantly improved living conditions.
The Israeli government says it intends to ease restrictions but wants Hamas to stop rocket attacks; Hamas has reduced attacks but some still fired.
Israel has curtailed airstrikes, but inter-factional fighting continues; previously Shifa Hospital received dead and injured daily, but now not.
People worry that unless sanctions are lifted, the fragile truce may collapse.

0-4716-3-1.subevent: Chile has been gripped by protests against high living costs and inequality for nearly two weeks, with demonstrators calling for President Sebastian Pinera to step down.
The protests began as a student-led demonstration after the government announced a metro fare increase, and outrage grew when the economy minister suggested those upset could wake up earlier.

Students conducted mass fare evasion and destroyed turnstiles; police used force, causing protests to spill into the streets, leading to burning of metro stations and supermarkets, and the declaration of a state of emergency.

The anger extends beyond metro prices to frustration with the cost of living, low wages, pensions, a poor public health system, and inequality; protesters demand pension system changes, a minimum wage increase, and a new constitution.
Pinera initially declared a state of emergency and deployed the military, but after a mass protest of over one million people, he lifted the state of emergency and replaced eight cabinet members.
Pinera proposed social reforms including a minimum wage increase and state pension rise, but critics said they did not go far enough; he also backed out of hosting the APEC and COP25 summits.
At least 20 civilians have died, over 1,200 have been injured, and thousands arrested; videos emerged showing military and police violence, prompting UN investigators to arrive.
Pinera’s concessions have failed to satisfy protesters, who vow to continue protesting until he steps down.

1-15327-3-t.subevent: A salesman arriving from Dubai felt sick at the airport in Trivandrum, was tested and then sent home to Chengala by ambulance.
Local village council and health centre contacted the salesman upon arrival, asked him to isolate himself in a shed; he later tested positive, recovered in hospital, and continued isolating at home.

The Chengala village council president said they prepared early; the council galvanized workers, opened a community kitchen for free lunches, and used helplines and WhatsApp to arrange housing for people in isolation.
Kerala imposed a lockdown a day before the national lockdown, did rigorous contact tracing, set up Covid-19 care centres, and health workers supported vulnerable people and provided counseling.
Experts attributed Kerala's success to its decentralized health care system and grassroots democracy, with village councils enforcing mass quarantine effectively.

Officials warned that claims of flattening the curve might be premature because testing was limited, antibody test kits were delayed, and fresh cases continued; Kerala got lucky with a younger infected population mostly from Gulf returnees.
Concerns remained about high rates of communicable diseases, comorbidities, and monsoon-triggered illnesses that could complicate diagnosis, as well as economic costs of vigilance.
Analysts said cases had slowed, recoveries were high, and mortality was low, but a doctor cautioned that they had only won the 'quarter-final' with more stages ahead.

0-4398-1-2.subevent: Ecuador's government declared a state of emergency to ensure citizens' security and avoid chaos after protests against a fuel price hike.
President Lenin Moreno ended 40-year-old fuel subsidies, causing diesel and petrol prices to more than double.
The fuel subsidies cost the government $1.3 billion annually.
Students and the transport sector led a national strike, blocking roads and bridges in Quito and Guayaquil.
Some protesters clashed with police, who fired tear gas; 19 people were arrested.
Protesters burned tyres and threw objects at police vans, drawing criticism from President Moreno.
The state of emergency allows the government to restrict freedoms and deploy the armed forces.
The elimination of subsidies is part of Moreno's plan to shore up the economy and ease debt, including an IMF loan deal signed in March.
Ecuador announced it was leaving OPEC to pump more oil and raise revenue.

24-31161-1-t.subevent: Laurel Hubbard failed to complete any of her three lifts in the women's over-87kg weightlifting competition at the Tokyo Olympics, eliminating her from medal contention.
China's Li Wenwen won the gold medal with a total of 320 kilograms, giving China its seventh gold in weightlifting at the Tokyo Games.
Emily Campbell won the silver medal, becoming the first British woman to win a weightlifting medal, and Sarah Robles won the bronze, becoming the first U.S. woman with two weightlifting medals.
Hubbard made a heart gesture to the audience and thanked the IOC, IWF, and the people of Japan for their support.
The IOC's 2015 recommendations for including transgender athletes were adopted by the IWF, requiring testosterone levels below a certain threshold, which Hubbard met.
The IOC will release a new framework for transgender athletes' eligibility in the coming months, based on newer scientific studies.
The New Zealand Olympic Committee acknowledged the sensitivity of gender identity in sport and committed to supporting all eligible athletes.
Earlier on Monday, Wang Zhouyu won the women's 87-kilogram weightlifting category for China.

0-4347-1-1.subevent: Bed Bath & Beyond Inc. increased the number of stores it expects to close in the fiscal year from 40 to 60.
Company officials said most closings are expected after the holiday shopping season in early 2020 during a quarterly earnings call.
Interim CEO Mary Winston said forty of the stores closing will be Bed Bath & Beyond stores and twenty will be stores in the company's other concepts.
Mary Winston stated that the closures will increase profitability and create a better balance between physical and digital presence.
As of the end of August, the company had 1,534 stores, including 993 Bed Bath & Beyond stores nationwide and in Canada.
Winston said there are plans to renegotiate all leases and remove $350 million of inventory from stores through markdowns and clearance events before the 2019 holiday season.
According to Coresight Research, nearly 8,600 store closures have been announced so far this year, up from around 5,900 in 2018.
Coresight estimates closures could reach 12,000 by the end of the year.

0-4569-4-1jpg.subevent: A former Fort Worth police officer, Aaron Dean, was indicted by a grand jury for murder in the death of Atatiana Jefferson.
Jefferson, 28, was shot and killed in October when Dean fired through a window.
Dean was arrested in October, but all police shootings go before a grand jury, which issues charges.
Dean was in the backyard of Jefferson's home when he shot her through a window after responding to a call about an open front door.
Dean resigned two days after the shooting and hours before being arrested and charged with murder.
Jefferson was inside a bedroom playing video games with her 8-year-old nephew; she grabbed her handgun after hearing noises outside.

Bodycam video showed Dean walking around, shining a flashlight into a window, shouting 'Put your hands up! Show me your hands!' and firing less than a second later, without identifying himself as an officer.

Less than three weeks after the murder, Judge David Hagerman issued a gag order preventing anyone connected with the case from making statements about witnesses, evidence or Dean's guilt or innocence.

2-34826-6-t.subevent: Turkey was the first country to recognize Kazakhstan.
Common historical and cultural ties form the basis of rapidly developing relations between Turkey and Kazakhstan.
After Kazakhstan's independence, many agreements and protocols were signed, and Kazakhstan became one of Turkey's most significant partners in the region.
A Strategic Partnership Agreement was signed during President Nursultan Nazarbayev's visit to Turkey in October 2009.

The High Level Strategic Cooperation Council was established during Prime Minister Recep Tayyip Erdoğan's visit to Kazakhstan in May 2012, with its first meeting in October 2012 and second in April 2015.
Bilateral trade volume reached nearly $3.9 billion in 2019, with a common target of $10 billion.
Turkish entrepreneurs are active in key sectors, and Turkish construction companies completed projects worth $23.5 billion by 2019.

Regional cooperation led to the institutionalization of the Summit of Turkic Speaking States, the establishment of the Turkic Council and TURKPA, and Kazakhstan hosting the International Turkic Academy.
About 8,000 students study at the campuses of International Hodja Ahmet Yesevi Turkish-Kazakh University.

12-wiki-img/8552-1/8552-1-1.subevent: Afghanistan announced on Monday that it would keep its main crossings with Iran open.
Officials said sealing the borders would drive returnees to illegal routes, increasing contamination risk, while official crossings allow medical checks and quarantining.
As of Monday, Afghanistan reported 141 positive cases and at least four deaths from COVID-19, with the virus brought by Afghan economic migrants fleeing Iran.
On average, at least 10,000 refugees have returned from Iran to Afghanistan every day over the past month through the official border crossing in Herat province.
Officials warned that closing the border would lead to more cases via illegal routes, as returnees would use human traffickers.
Authorities increased preventive measures along the border, including checking all returnees and isolating those affected, but cited illegal crossings as the main challenge.
Afghanistan extended the lockdown in Herat province by three more weeks and enforced a curfew in Kabul.
Residents expressed concern about the spread of the virus and the influx of returnees from Iran.

2-34513-5-t.subevent: Lebanese Prime Minister Najib Mikati announced on Twitter that Friday would be a day of public mourning for those killed in violence in Beirut on Thursday.

Six Shi'ites were shot dead in Beirut in an attack on supporters of Hezbollah and an allied Lebanese party who were gathering to demand the removal of the judge investigating last year's Beirut port blast.

6-18755-14-1.subevent: The Madras High Court’s Madurai Bench lifted the ban on TikTok subject to conditions.
The bench vacated its interim order banning the app, subject to conditions that pornographic videos will not be uploaded.
TikTok issued a statement expressing gladness and welcoming the decision.
Earlier, the high court issued an interim order to the central government banning downloading of the app in India and restricting media from telecasting videos taken using the app.
Tamil Nadu’s Information Technology Minister M. Manikandan said the state would write to the central government seeking a ban on the app.
The high court appointed leading lawyer Arvind Datar as an independent counsel to the court.
The Supreme Court on April 22 asked the Madras High Court to decide on TikTok’s plea for interim relief by April 24, failing which the ban would stand lifted.
TikTok stated it was committed to continuously enhancing its safety features and expressed gratitude.

1-16189-3-1.subevent: Consumer prices rose 800 percent and the economy contracted 18.6 percent in 2016 according to preliminary central bank figures.
The central bank stopped releasing quarterly and monthly economic indicators.
The oil sector shrank 12.7 percent and the non-oil sector shrank 19.5 percent in 2016.
The inflation and GDP figures could be changed during the approval process by the central bank board.
In 2015, inflation was 180.9 percent and the economy contracted 5.7 percent.
President Maduro accused opposition-linked businesses of creating economic problems, blamed speculation for inflation, and claimed minimum wage increases of 454 percent in 2016 were above inflation.
Currency controls left businesses unable to obtain dollars, causing shortages and prompting Venezuelans to cross borders into Brazil and Colombia to buy groceries.
Investor concern about Venezuela's ability to service its debt made its bonds among the highest-yielding emerging market securities, but Maduro dismissed rumors of default.

32-2285-2-1.subevent: A billboard before Game 3 showed Kawhi Leonard with the message 'The King of the North is Coming,' and a Warriors fan snickered at it.
The Raptors went up 3-1 in the NBA Finals and celebrated after Game 4 at Oracle Arena, as many Warriors fans left early and Raptors players showed little emotion.
The Raptors became the 35th team to hold a 3-1 Finals lead; only the 2016 Warriors have lost from that position.
Kawhi Leonard recorded his 14th 30-point playoff performance in Game 4, joining Michael Jordan, Hakeem Olajuwon, Allen Iverson, Kobe Bryant, and LeBron James.
The Raptors' supporting cast and big men outperformed the Warriors' bigs, while Kevin Durant remained sidelined and Steph Curry's best Finals performance came in a Game 3 loss.
Raptors coach Nick Nurse said all Finals games are critical, and noted that his team has won five of six meetings with the Warriors this season, including 13 of 16 quarters in the series.

FiveThirtyEight initially gave the Raptors a 12 percent title chance, but after taking a 3-1 lead, Golden State's odds dropped to 11 percent; Steph Curry called it 'not a good feeling' and Draymond Green said 'This sucks.'
Nurse said the Raptors 'flipped a switch' after Game 2 against Orlando in the first round, and they have been the best team in the playoffs, overcoming doubts against the Magic, Sixers, and Bucks.
After Game 4, Kyle Lowry paused to take a selfie with a young Warriors fan, symbolizing the Raptors capturing everyone's attention.

9-21834-8-1.subevent: President Trump declared Sunday a National Day of Prayer and millions of Americans attended religious services online due to social distancing.
Megachurches streamed their Sunday service online; Trump tweeted that he was watching a service by Pastor Jentezen Franklin and thanked him.
Pastor Jentezen Franklin preached a message titled 'Choose faith over fear' to an empty auditorium viewed by nearly 200,000 people.
Greg Laurie's church saw over 230,000 online attendees and over 1,400 people committed to follow Jesus.
LifeBridge Community Church offered online services with curbside prayer, and Dr. Alveda King urged Americans to 'Don't panic. Pray.'

Smaller churches faced decisions on services; at St. Philip African Methodist Episcopal Church, about 100 congregants attended, and Rev. William Watley said they would follow directives and encouraged hand washing.

Christian author Lee Strobel tweeted over 300 salvations through online services, and religious leaders took unprecedented actions, including Catholic bishops dispensing Mass attendance and the Mormon Church halting all worship services worldwide.
The Vatican announced all public Masses in Italy are forbidden, likely extending beyond April 3, and Pope Francis visited St. Mary Major Basilica to pray for the sick.
Over 6,470 people have died globally from the coronavirus, with most people recovering in two to six weeks.

17-28164-3-1.subevent: Dale Coyne Racing announced a collaboration with Rick Ware Racing for the full-time #51 car and the part-time #52 car, with Rick Ware as co-entrant for both.
Ed Jones will pilot the #18 Dale Coyne Racing with Vasser Sullivan-Honda.
Dale Coyne said they met Rick Ware at the 2020 Indianapolis 500 and have discussed collaboration since.
The primary sponsor of the #51 car will be announced in February, and the driver for that car is expected to be announced next week.
Ex-Formula 1 driver Romain Grosjean is the favorite for the #51 seat, but his participation in oval races is uncertain.
If Grosjean does not compete in the oval races, JR Hildebrand could replace him, but Hildebrand is unavailable for the Indy 500 due to his commitment with Dreyer & Reinbold Racing.
Rick Ware commented that the collaboration is a logical step and he looks forward to a competitive 2021.
Rick Ware Racing fields four charters in the NASCAR Cup Series and has competed in various other series since 2000.
The RWR Eurasia entry will compete in the LMP2 class at the Rolex 24 at Daytona.

11-22309-3-t.subevent: Clergy groups in Muskogee are working to establish a fund to support a local mother who lost five of her children in a shooting.
Police say 25-year-old Jarron Deajon Pridgeon shot Brittany Anderson, five of her children, and his brother in a Muskogee home on Feb. 2.
Anderson is recovering from the shooting, but the other victims died.
Muskogee Mayor Marlon Coleman announced plans for the fund Wednesday and is asking the community to also support first responders.
Coleman plans to sign a proclamation in the next few days to establish March as "Community Care Month for First Responders."
Coleman says several first responders are getting therapy or counseling because of the shooting and he wants the community to support them.
Anderson is out of the hospital resting, and funeral details for the children have yet to be announced.
Coleman plans to announce details on the fund to support the family soon.

0-4832-2-t.subevent: The Premier League suspended its 2019/20 season on 13 March 2020 due to the coronavirus pandemic.
The league worked with professional football, the Government, public agencies, and stakeholders to plan the season's resumption.
Stage 1 of 'Project Restart' allowed small-group training from 19 May 2020.
Stage 2 began on 27 May 2020, allowing contact training.
The 2019/20 season resumed on 17 June 2020 with matches behind closed doors.
Strict medical protocols, risk assessments, and regular testing were implemented for the return to training and matches.
The 2020/21 season started with matches behind closed doors, with a brief period of limited fans in December 2020 and at all grounds in May 2021.
The 2021/22 season began with full stadiums, but the Premier League created matchday protocols and protocols for training and matchdays to keep everyone safe.

1-15241-6-4.subevent: Syrian firefighters and army helicopters battled forest fires for a seventh consecutive day in government-held areas.
Iran sent a firefighting plane carrying 40 tons of water to help fight the fires in Latakia and Hama provinces.
State media published images of billowing smoke above tree tops and charred vegetation.
Forestry official Hassan Fares said numerous fires had been put out but some continued to rage in areas of Latakia.
The agriculture ministry said steep terrain prevented fire trucks from reaching fire-hit areas quickly.
There was no immediate data on the total area affected.
Hama governor Mohammed Al-Hazouri said the blaze had ravaged eight square kilometers of agricultural land in his province.
Summer fires are common in Syria, but residents said this year's fires were worse than usual.
Syria's war has killed over 380,000 people, displaced millions, and decimated the country's economy.

1-14808-1-t.subevent: Businessman and TV host Zef Eisenberg died while attempting to break a British land speed record at Elvington Airfield.
He lost control of his Porsche 911 Turbo S at Elvington Airfield and died at the scene.
North Yorkshire Police confirmed he died during a British Land Speed record attempt.
Eisenberg had set dozens of speed records on bikes, cars, and quad bikes, according to UK Motorsport.
Elvington Airfield has been the scene of notable accidents, including Eisenberg's 2016 crash and Richard Hammond's near-fatal crash in 2006.
Motorsport UK expressed deep sadness and announced an investigation into the accident.
Motorsport UK stated that Eisenberg, aged 47, was a Guernsey-based businessman, television presenter, and a much-loved member of the motorsport community.
It said he amassed over 70 British, World, UKTA, ACU and Guinness speed records, received the Simms Medal in 2019, and leaves behind his partner and two children.
Eisenberg earned a world record in 2015 for reaching 225 mph on a turbine-powered motorbike.
He was attempting to break the British land speed record of 207.6 mph set by Tony Densham in 1970.

1-wiki-img/15302-2/15302-2-1.subevent: Armenia's forces hit Ganja, Azerbaijan's second-largest city, killing and injuring dozens of Azerbaijani civilians, less than a day after a humanitarian ceasefire between Yerevan and Baku came into effect.

Hikmat Hajiyev accused Armenia of hiding behind the ceasefire to attack civilians and reported that the missile attack destroyed three residential buildings, killing at least seven civilians and wounding 33.
The humanitarian ceasefire reached on Saturday called for the exchange of hostages and dead bodies, and the attack on Ganja was the second of its kind since October 4.

Hajiyev stated that the city of Mingachevir was also hit by a Smerch heavy multiple rocket launcher received by Armenia during the ceasefire, and accused Atlantis Armenian Airlines of transporting missiles and missile systems on civilian aircraft.

The conflict escalated after September 27 when Armenia's troops began shelling military and civilian positions of Azerbaijan, leading to the longest and fiercest fighting between the two countries since the 1994 ceasefire.

As of Saturday, Armenia confirmed the deaths of 405 servicemen, while Azerbaijan said 2,300 Armenian servicemen were killed or wounded, and overall Azerbaijani civilian casualties reached 40 dead and over 200 injured.

The Nagorno-Karabakh conflict, stemming from anti-Azerbaijan sentiments in Armenia in 1988, resulted in Armenia occupying 20 percent of Azerbaijan's internationally recognized territories after the Soviet Union's dissolution, displacing one million ethnic Azerbaijanis and killing 30,000.
Armenia continues to defy four UN Security Council resolutions on the withdrawal of its occupying forces from Azerbaijani lands and the return of internally displaced Azerbaijanis.

6-19298-5-10.subevent: Kumbh Mela is the largest peaceful congregation of pilgrims on earth, during which participants bathe in a sacred river.
Devotees believe that by bathing in the Ganges one is freed from sins and the cycle of birth and death.
Millions of people, including ascetics, saints, sadhus, aspirants, and visitors, reach the place without any invitation.
The festival is held at Allahabad, Haridwar, Ujjain, and Nasik every four years by rotation.
It is attended by millions irrespective of caste, creed, or gender, but primary bearers belong to akhadas, ashrams, religious organizations, or individuals living on alms.
Kumbh Mela plays a central spiritual role in India, exerting a mesmeric influence on ordinary Indians.
The event encapsulates the science of astronomy, astrology, spirituality, ritualistic traditions, and social and cultural customs, making it extremely rich in knowledge.
As it is held in four different cities, it involves different social and cultural activities, making it culturally diverse.

Knowledge and skills are transmitted through ancient religious manuscripts, oral traditions, historical travelogues, and texts by eminent historians, but the teacher-student relationship of sadhus remains the most important method.

5-5883-1-1.subevent: The European Space Agency is starting a regular series of small science missions, called S-Class missions.
The first winning S-Class idea will receive 50 million euros and be readied for launch in 2017.
This marks a departure from ESA's typical large missions; the agency aims to encourage young scientists and smaller member states.
Prof. Mark McCaughrean said the program will train young scientists and allow smaller states to lead missions, and called for innovative low-cost ideas.
Expressions of interest must be submitted by 23 March, followed by a defined proposal in June; a clutch of best ideas will be selected for study in November, with a winner chosen 12 months later.
S-Class missions must fit within ESA's Cosmic Vision, and national governments will likely fund instrument development.
Realistic mission concepts include compact space telescopes or fundamental physics experiments, not deep-space probes or Mars landers.
Examples include the Lares spacecraft launched in February on Vega rocket to study frame-dragging, and ESA's Proba-2 satellite with Swap imager that tracked a solar storm last week.

In contrast, ESA is about to select its next large L-Class mission from three competing ideas: a big X-ray telescope, a probe to Jupiter and its moons, and a gravitational wave detector, costing about a billion euros.

26-13936-2-1.subevent: Millions of students, workers and scientists came together at the global climate strikes last week.
Over 7.6 million people held demonstrations, making it one of the biggest global demonstrations in history.
The 350 Movement reported more than 6,100 events were held in 185 countries with support from trade unions, civil society organizations, companies, and websites.
Celebrities such as Leonardo DiCaprio, Keith Richards, Mick Jagger, and Chris Hemsworth supported the strike on social media.
Italy, Germany, Canada, the U.S., and Spain were the five countries with the most attendees.
Young climate activists gave powerful speeches while oil company CEOs met with government representatives to lobby on climate policy.
The movement stressed the importance of meeting Paris Agreement goals and cutting emissions while criticizing big fossil fuel companies for profiting from coal, oil, and gas.

0-4325-2-1.subevent: The opioid crisis is worsening due to new drugs like fentanyl.
A photograph shows a lethal dose of heroin (30mg) compared to a lethal dose of fentanyl (3mg).
The CDC states that fentanyl is up to 100 times more potent than morphine.
Drug users often don't know when their heroin is laced with fentanyl, risking accidental overdose.
Dealers add fentanyl to improve potency but lack fine-tuned measuring equipment.
Street fentanyl is made in clandestine labs, is less pure, and its effects are more unpredictable.
Tim Pifer, lab director, said users don't know what they're taking and compared it to a loaded gun.
New Hampshire saw 439 drug overdoses in 2015, most opioid-related, with about 70% of opioid deaths involving fentanyl; 200 deadly overdoses so far this year.
Fentanyl was originally used as an anesthetic, then for pain relief; with professional equipment it has a wide therapeutic index.
Differences in chemical structures cause fentanyl to bind faster and tighter to the mu opioid receptor than morphine.

3-17502-3-t.subevent: Portugal's Catholic bishops suspended public Masses from Jan. 23 due to the extreme gravity of the coronavirus crisis, calling it a moral imperative.
Portugal is experiencing a surge in COVID-19 deaths, with 609,000 cases and 9,920 deaths as of Jan. 22; this is the second suspension, the first being in March 2020.
The suspension includes public Masses, catechesis, and other gatherings; priests were asked to livestream Masses.
Earlier in January, the bishops called for suspension or postponement of baptisms, confirmations, and marriages.
Funerals may be celebrated according to May 2020 norms requiring social distancing.
A Lenten retreat for bishops scheduled for Feb. 22-26 was canceled.
The Shrine of Our Lady of Fatima will broadcast three Masses and two rosaries daily during the suspension via its website.
Shrine rector Fr. Carlos Cabecinhas acknowledged that following online is not the same but is the only possible way now.

26-14496-4-1.subevent: Sebastien Buemi set the fastest lap of 3m19.719s in the #8 Toyota just before the two-hour mark, leading Mike Conway's 3m20.611s in the #7 Toyota.
Nathanael Berthon placed the #3 Rebellion third, 3.456s behind the leader.
The #4 ByKolles entry was fourth in LMP1 but slower than the leading LMP2 car.
Rebellion's #1 car spent most of the session in the garage for an engine change.

The fastest six cars in each class will progress to Friday's Hyperpole shootout.

1-15227-1-1.subevent: Pakistan blocked the Chinese social media app TikTok due to failure to fully comply with instructions to develop an effective mechanism to control unlawful content.
The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority said it received complaints about 'immoral and indecent' content on the platform.
The PTA issued a final notice to TikTok and gave it time to respond and comply with instructions, but the company failed to fully comply.
Shortly after the ban, TikTok began to show a blank interface with no text or images loading.
The PTA left the door open for TikTok's return, stating it would review its decision if TikTok develops a mechanism to moderate content.
In July, the PTA issued a 'final warning' to TikTok to remove 'obscene and immoral content.'
Pakistani TikTok celebrity Hareem Shah said the government's reasons for the ban were 'unfounded' and that such actions could encroach on creative liberties.
Hareem Shah described TikTok as a good app for entertainment that showcases the talent of Pakistani youth.
TikTok is the third-most downloaded app in Pakistan over the past year, with 39 million downloads, and was previously banned by India and the United States.

1-15874-5-1.subevent: A new mission proposal suggests a relocatable lander called Dragonfly could explore Saturn's moon Titan.
Dragonfly would investigate potentially habitable sites on Titan where methane and ethane rain and flow.
Dragonfly would take advantage of Titan's low gravity and thick atmosphere to visit multiple sites over several years, recharging between brief flights.
Elizabeth Turtle presented the Dragonfly concept at the Lunar and Planetary Sciences Conference.
Turtle noted that Titan's methane and ethane rivers provide a unique opportunity to explore prebiotic chemistry.
Turtle stated that Titan's thick atmosphere enables the mission's travel capability.

8-6386-5-t.subevent: A video published Thursday showed how the Houston Astros allegedly used two different whistling noises to signal to batters during the 2017 World Series, breaking down at-bats from several players.

Former Astros pitcher Mike Fiers and other unnamed sources revealed to The Athletic that the team used a sophisticated sign-stealing system with a camera in centerfield and a monitor in the clubhouse.
Two sources told The Athletic that the sign-stealing extended into the 2017 postseason, but another denied it went on that long.
A 2017 DVD commemorating the Astros' first World Series championship showed a table, chairs and a TV in the clubhouse which appeared to be the area where a team employee would alert batters.
On Sunday, Twitter user Jomboy brought to light the team's alleged cheating setup from the championship DVD.
MLB commissioner Rob Manfred said Thursday an investigation was underway covering 2017-2019 and that the Astros were the only team being investigated for now.
Manfred stated that there should be firm, serious disciplinary action to discourage this behavior.
Astros owner Jim Crane declined to comment on the allegations.

0-4930-1-3.subevent: A police helicopter crashed through the roof of the Clutha Vaults pub in Glasgow during a live music event, with at least three feared dead and dozens hospitalized.
The Eurocopter EC135 T2 operated by Police Scotland, carrying two police officers and a civilian pilot, came down just before 10:30pm, and a major incident was declared.
Scotland's first minister Alex Salmond tweeted that fatalities were likely, confirming the helicopter was a police one and that rescue efforts were in full operation.
Assistant Chief Officer Lewis Ramsay of the Scottish Fire and Rescue Service said crews were treating the incident as a rescue operation with 125 firefighters and numerous casualties.
Labour MP Jim Murphy described a human chain of members of the public helping to get people out of the building.
Witness Wesley McEwan said he could see two people in the cockpit through the shattered windscreen and people trapped under the helicopter.
Witness Grace MacLean heard a whoosh noise, saw the roof start to come down, and said people were screaming but others helped direct them to the door.
Editor Gordon Smart heard a misfiring engine and saw the helicopter falling from a great height at great speed, like a stone, with no explosion.
Police set up cordons and dozens of people were taken to a nearby Holiday Inn; the band Esperanza was identified as the act playing at the time.

Police Scotland Deputy Chief Constable Rose Fitzpatrick confirmed the helicopter crashed at 10:25pm, stated the rescue operation was ongoing, and announced a joint investigation with the Air Accident Investigation Branch.

0-4551-2-t.subevent: The Turkish judiciary attempted to close down the governing Justice and Development Party (AKP).
The current political tensions in Turkey date back further than the recent attempt to close the AKP.
The tensions are linked to broader issues of secularism versus Islamism.
The situation may have implications for Turkey’s EU accession candidate status.
The outcome of the court ruling will signal the beginning of a new era in Turkish politics.
The only way out of the current political impasse seems to be the adoption of a conciliatory attitude by all parties concerned.

This conciliatory attitude seems only a remote possibility given a governing party whose democratic credentials are in question, an opposition that provides no credible alternative policy, and a judiciary that has not fully purged itself of entrenched beliefs.

13-wiki-img/25021-4/25021-4-1.subevent: Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly said measures have been taken to compensate the victims of the Sohag train collision and their families, as well as precautions to avoid such accidents.

Solidarity Minister Nevine el-Kabbag said President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi demanded that compensations are dispensed promptly, as well as providing medical, psychological and social care for the victims.

The family of a victim killed in the accident is entitled to L.E. 100,000, and a victim who has incurred a disability will be compensated commensurately with the injury from L.E. 100,000 to L.E. 40,000, with a lifetime pension available for the victims.
A total of L.E. 20,000 have been available for the families of the deceased since Saturday as part of prompt compensation, and L.E. 5,000-10,000 for the injured.
Al-Azhar and NGOs have expressed willingness to help with the social assistance of the victims and their families in terms of education, work and psychological welfare.
Minister of Health Hala Zayed said the death toll reported at the time of the accident was not accurate because people in post-concussion coma were initially reported dead.
Zayed added that 20 people were in such coma, and the latest death toll stands at 19 after it was first reported to be more than 30.
Zayed also said the first ambulance arrived at the scene five minutes after the accident, praising the locals for helping emergency crews.

3-18343-1-t.subevent: Pitt's men's basketball and football programs were placed on three years' probation, and former basketball coach Kevin Stallings received a three-year show-cause order for instructing non-coaching staff to perform coaching duties.
Pitt self-reported the violation prior to the NCAA investigation.
Athletic director Heather Lyke released a statement expressing commitment to compliance.
Stallings developed an alert system and ordered deletion of video to avoid detection, and despite warnings, he did not cease violations.
Under the show-cause order, if Stallings is hired within three years, he must be suspended from 30% of the first season.
The former director of basketball operations produced personalized recruiting videos for 12 prospects and later refused to participate in an enforcement interview.

Football coach Pat Narduzzi was present at a practice where three former quality control staff performed coaching duties; the violation went undetected due to a music system, and Narduzzi received a show-cause order withholding him from two days of practice.
Narduzzi issued a statement acknowledging his responsibility.

Pitt received a $5,000 fine from both budgets and a three-year show-cause for the former director of basketball operations, and men's basketball had a reduction in countable coaches for 16 hours while football had a reduction for four days and removal of two quality control staff for three days.

1-16165-3-2.subevent: The Australian Grand Prix was cancelled due to coronavirus concerns.
A McLaren team member tested positive for Covid-19, leading McLaren to withdraw from the race.
The FIA and Formula 1 convened a meeting of the team principals after McLaren's withdrawal.
Mercedes requested cancellation of the race, and Ferrari issued a statement supporting the decision.
Victoria state premier Daniel Andrews said the race would have to be behind closed doors if it were held.
Fans arriving at Albert Park were refused entry as confusion surrounded the event.
Lewis Hamilton expressed surprise and concern about holding the race with fans present.
The other seven F1 personnel tested negative for coronavirus.
The cancellation could affect the Bahrain and Vietnam Grands Prix and the start of the season.

9-20780-1-1.subevent: Google suspended the Parler social networking app from its Play Store until it adds robust content moderation.
Apple gave Parler 24 hours to submit a detailed moderation plan or be removed from the App Store.
Parler CEO John Matze said Apple was applying standards to Parler that it did not apply to itself and that the companies were attacking civil liberties.
Plans for the protests in Washington DC that ended in the storming of the Capitol were widely shared on Parler.
Google cited its policy against apps that promote violence and gave examples of posts on Parler, including one about coordinated hits and another promoting a 'Million Militia March'.
Google stated that it requires apps to implement robust moderation for egregious content and suspended Parler's listings due to the ongoing public safety threat.
Apple cited the mob storming the US Capitol and demanded that Parler remove all objectionable content and submit a written moderation plan within 24 hours.
Parler was founded in 2018 as a free-speech alternative and has attracted right-leaning users, including prominent supporters of Donald Trump.
Matze said that by holding Parler responsible for all user-generated content, Apple must also be responsible for all actions taken with iPhones.

0-4403-2-2.subevent: French interior minister Christophe Castaner said signs of Islamist radicalisation should trigger an 'automatic alert', deploring failings that allowed a knifeman to kill four police colleagues.
Mickaël Harpon was shot dead on Thursday after stabbing colleagues at the Paris police headquarters.
Castaner said police should have investigated Harpon's suspicious behaviour in 2015, but no formal concerns were raised.
Castaner revealed that in 2015 colleagues had spoken about Harpon's praise for the Charlie Hebdo attack and his changed behaviour towards women, but no concerns were formally reported.
Castaner brushed off calls for his resignation, pledging to 'tighten the net' to pick up suspicious signs and rectify the malfunctioning alert system.
Anti-terror investigators took over the inquiry on Friday; it was initially regarded as a criminal matter.
Harpon, an IT expert who had contact with the Salafist movement, exchanged 33 text messages with his wife on Thursday morning including religious phrases; his wife was questioned and released.

Harpon bought two knives half an hour before the attack, stabbed three people in two offices and two women on a stairway, killing three men and one woman, and seriously injuring a fifth person, before being shot dead.

5-6042-3-t.subevent: His Holiness Patriarch Kirill noted that Patriarch Bartholomew's invasion into Ukraine generated schisms in Universal Orthodoxy.
Patriarch Kirill said he believes Patriarch Bartholomew was guided not by his own reason or will.
Patriarch Kirill rejected the argument that Patriarch Bartholomew could not act otherwise due to external pressure, citing the Russian Church's experience under an atheistic state.
Patriarch Kirill recalled that there were martyrs and confessors among the Patriarchs of Constantinople, and that Constantinople was a stronghold of Orthodoxy.
Patriarch Kirill stated that the Patriarch of Constantinople has lapsed into schism by taking communion with schismatics and recognizing self-ordained clergy.

Patriarch Kirill stressed that they must seek to overcome the crisis in inter-Orthodox relations pastorally and humanly, because there are brothers and sisters in countries influenced by the Patriarch of Constantinople.
Patriarch Kirill noted that the Department for External Church Relations has work to do to help Universal Orthodoxy come out of the grave crisis.
Patriarch Kirill emphasized the importance of common solidarity and showing love for one another to strengthen Universal Orthodoxy.

9-21110-8-2.subevent: YouTube blamed a tech issue for accidentally censoring 'hundreds of thousands' of LGBT videos.
Controversy arose earlier this year over the site's Restricted Mode feature, introduced to filter potentially inappropriate content for young people.
Some of the site's biggest LGBT content creators spoke out after seemingly-innocuous videos about sexuality or sex education were flagged as restricted.
In a blog post, YouTube said the automated filters for restricted mode had wrongfully impacted 'hundreds of thousands' of videos on LGBT issues.
YouTube announced they fixed an issue that was incorrectly filtering videos, making 12 million additional videos including hundreds of thousands featuring LGBTQ+ content available in Restricted Mode.
YouTube started providing a form to allow creators and viewers to report videos they believed were being inappropriately excluded from Restricted Mode.

YouTube published guidelines for restricted mode, clarifying that some educational conversations about sexual education may be included but overly detailed conversations about sex will likely be removed.
YouTube explained that its system sometimes makes mistakes in understanding context and nuances, and acknowledged the need to do better.

0-4912-1-1.subevent: A landslide caused by torrential rainfall in Bafoussam, Cameroon, killed dozens of people.
Rescue teams searched the rubble of destroyed homes for survivors.
Governor Awa Fonka Augustine warned residents to leave the dangerous area.
Augustine reported that the death toll had risen from 13 to at least 34, with a dozen people severely wounded and the potential for more deaths.
The state-run Cameroon Tribune reported that 33 bodies had been recovered.
Police searched for dozens of people reported missing.
It was feared that at least two pregnant women were killed; Pierre Kemvhe said his pregnant wife was missing.
Heavy rains continued, causing severe flooding in the Central African Republic that displaced nearly 30,000 people and in South Sudan affecting nearly one million.

22-wiki-img/3685-3/3685-3-4.subevent: Marine Le Pen, riding a growing populist insurgency, may top the first round of France's presidential election on 23 April, with under-30s in France being more nationalistic than the general population.

Génération Identitaire (GI) specializes in publicity stunts filmed and posted online to reclaim French territory from migrants, and its leader Pierre Larti engaged in a verbal confrontation with a North African man while handing out flyers in Paris.
GI is sprouting branches across Europe, viewing the continent as a battleground between European and Islamic culture.
Jean-Yves Le Gallou produced a video 'Being European' that has been viewed over 3.2 million times, and identitarians have thrived on the web, with Fdesouche getting about 3 million views per month.

Alain Soral's website Égalité et Reconciliation has more readers than Fdesouche and is France's most popular political website; Soral rejects accusations of anti-Semitism and is regularly prosecuted for incitement.

At Sciences Po, Eurosceptic students set up a club 'Critique of European Reason' (CRE) to create a Eurosceptic safe space, and members regard uncontrolled migration and trade flows as a source of social disintegration.

Students like Kevin and Ugo Iannuzzi shared feelings of anti-white racism and insecurity in immigrant suburbs, leading them to support the FN or hard-left candidates, and Alexandre Devecchio called this generation the 'Zemmour generation' that feels let down.

1-16497-7-t.subevent: WFSA is working with its global membership to curate and disseminate up-to-date COVID-19 guidance for anaesthesia and perioperative care providers.
WFSA requests that additional resources be shared by contacting Francis Peel.
WFSA draws attention to the risk for anaesthesiologists and the importance of appropriate precautions when providing respiratory care and intubation for COVID-19 patients.
WFSA publishes a statement on healthcare provider safety and wellbeing during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Multiple organizations, including APSF, ASA, IARS, and WFSA, release guidance on anaesthesia and perioperative care for COVID-19, covering airway management, obstetric anaesthesia, and low-resource settings.
WFSA member societies, such as the Indian Society of Anaesthesiologists and the South African Society of Anaesthesiologists, issue advisories.
Resources in French, Spanish, and Portuguese are compiled from various societies.
General information and training resources from WHO, CDC, and MSF are included.

0-4799-1-t.subevent: CPS canceled classes for Thursday, the sixth day without school, as CTU had not scheduled a House of Delegates vote to end the strike.
Thousands of teachers and school employees marched downtown Wednesday, causing street closures, and rallied outside Mayor Lightfoot's budget address.
CTU said the event was picket lines shifting to the Loop in a joint effort with SEIU Local 73 and allied organizations.
Lightfoot delivered her budget address, unveiling proposals to help fill an $838 million budget gap.
The march and rally shifted to a sit-in on city streets as Lightfoot's address began.
Negotiations continued on the fifth day of canceled classes.
